speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned having a fever and abdominal tenderness after giving birth; can you tell me exactly when your delivery occurred and how high your temperature has reached? Also, have you noticed any foul-smelling vaginal discharge or excessive bleeding?

speaker: Patient
text: 24-year-old woman. The patient is in the postpartum period after delivering an 11 pound boy vaginally at 40 weeks gestation. She experienced a prolonged course during labor. She reports increased frequency of urination and uterine tenderness. She also mentions a decrease in bowel sounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Postpartum endometritis with possible urinary tract involvement. The combination of fever, uterine tenderness, and foul-smelling discharge (implied by the clinical picture of postpartum infection) strongly suggests endometritis. However, the presence of urinary frequency and decreased bowel sounds raises concern for concurrent urinary tract infection or bowel pathology. Given the 11-pound baby and prolonged labor, we must rule out other complications. I will now order a urinalysis and complete blood count (CBC) to assess for bacteriuria and leukocytosis. REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis, CBC, and Blood Culture. REQUEST IMAGES: Pelvic Ultrasound.
